# Aingworth

> Brand authority and AI visibility consulting from Lucy Aingworth, author of *Become the Answer: How Brands Build Authority in the Age of AI*. Aingworth helps founders, CMOs, and executives build the Clarity, Credibility, and Earned Authority that AI systems use to decide who to cite and recommend - the Recognition Triangle framework at the center of the practice.

Lucy Aingworth is an AI visibility consultant, brand authority consultant, and generative engine optimisation (GEO) consultant with over a decade of experience in SEO, CRO, paid media, and digital strategy across global markets. She now focuses specifically on helping brands become recognized and cited by AI search and answer systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI. She works with clients internationally.

The practice is built on a set of named frameworks and concepts introduced in *Become the Answer*: the Recognition Triangle (Clarity, Credibility, Earned Authority), the Authority Method (Diagnose, Define, Build, Distribute, Refine), the Recognition Economy, the Machine Gatekeeper, Authority Debt, brand hallucination, and the composite picture.

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://aingworth.com/): Overview of Aingworth, the Recognition Triangle framework, and the case for brand authority in AI-mediated search.
- [Services](https://aingworth.com/services/): Consulting, coaching, speaking, and workshop services, typically starting with an AI Visibility Audit.
- [The Recognition Diagnostic](https://aingworth.com/diagnostic/): A free 15-question self-assessment that identifies which of six Recognition Triangle patterns - The Promising Claim, The Hidden Expert, The Validated Generalist, The Strong Foundation, The Recognized Authority, or The Decaying Authority - currently describes a brand, with tailored next steps for each.
- [The Aingworth Glossary](https://aingworth.com/glossary/): 91 defined terms covering recognition, authority, and AI-mediated discovery, organized into seven layers: Recognition and Authority, AI-Mediated Discovery, Retrieval and Evidence and Consensus, Search and SEO and Generative Optimization, AI and Search Infrastructure, Content and Authority Strategy, and Measurement and AI Visibility. Each term is labeled by provenance, so Aingworth's own concepts are distinguished from established industry and technical vocabulary. Terms Aingworth defines include Recognition, the Recognition Economy, the Recognition Triangle, Clarity, Credibility, Earned Authority, Brand Authority Infrastructure, the Authority Method, Authority Debt, Authority Decay, the Recognition Gap, Recognition and Authority Signals, Brand Representation, the Composite Picture, the Machine Gatekeeper, Brand Hallucination, the Recognition Diagnostic, the Recognition Patterns, Foundational and Signal and Confirmation Assets, Consensus Over Rankings, AI-Mediated Discovery, Retrievability, Corroboration, Model Consensus, and Signal Consistency. The page carries schema.org DefinedTermSet markup containing every definition.
  - [Recognition & Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/): The core Aingworth vocabulary: Recognition, the Recognition Triangle, Clarity, Credibility, Earned Authority, Brand Authority Infrastructure, the Authority Method, Authority Debt, and the rest of the concepts set out in Become the Answer.
    - [Authority Debt](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/authority-debt/): Authority Debt: The accumulated cost of chasing visibility metrics instead of building authority signals.
    - [Authority Decay](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/authority-decay/): Authority Decay: The gradual weakening of authority as evidence ages and references disappear.
    - [Authority Method](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/authority-method/): The Authority Method is the five-stage process for building brand authority that AI systems cite: Diagnose, Define, Build, Distribute, Refine.
    - [Authority Signal](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/authority-signal/): Authority Signal: A piece of evidence that establishes a brand's expertise or standing.
    - [Brand Authority Infrastructure](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/brand-authority-infrastructure/): Brand Authority Infrastructure: The structured system of evidence and signals that makes a brand credible wherever it is evaluated.
    - [Brand Hallucination](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/brand-hallucination/): Brand Hallucination: When an AI system confidently describes a brand inaccurately.
    - [Brand Representation](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/brand-representation/): Brand Representation: How a brand is described and understood across the sources that influence discovery.
    - [Clarity](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/clarity/): Clarity: The unambiguous definition of who a brand is, what it does, and who it serves.
    - [Community Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/community-authority/): Community Authority: The Earned Authority layer built from forums, reviews, and practitioner discussion.
    - [Composite Picture](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/composite-picture/): The Composite Picture is the aggregate impression AI systems assemble about a brand from every signal across the web, accurate or not.
    - [Consensus Over Rankings](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/consensus-over-rankings/): Consensus Over Rankings: Being confirmed by many independent sources beats ranking first on one.
    - [Credibility](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/credibility/): Credibility is what can be verified: the proof, track record, and validation that let people and AI systems trust the claims a brand makes about itself.
    - [Earned Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/earned-authority/): Earned Authority: What others say about a brand when it is not in the room.
    - [Expert Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/expert-authority/): Expert Authority is the Earned Authority layer built from expert sources: analyst reports, academic citations, and industry publications.
    - [Foundational, Signal & Confirmation Assets](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/foundational-signal-confirmation-assets/): Foundational, Signal & Confirmation Assets: Aingworth's taxonomy for what a brand actually needs to build.
    - [Machine Gatekeeper](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/machine-gatekeeper/): The Machine Gatekeeper is the layer of AI systems that now sits between a brand and its audience, deciding who gets cited, recommended, and trusted.
    - [Recognition](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition/): Recognition: Being correctly understood and recalled by the people and systems that shape discovery.
    - [Recognition Diagnostic](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-diagnostic/): Recognition Diagnostic: Aingworth's free fifteen-question assessment across the three conditions.
    - [Recognition Economy](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-economy/): Recognition Economy: The shift from competing to be seen to competing to be recognized and retrieved.
    - [Recognition Gap](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-gap/): Recognition Gap: The distance between how well a brand understands its value and how well others do.
    - [Recognition Patterns](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-patterns/): Recognition Patterns: The six diagnostic outcomes, from Promising Claim to Recognized Authority.
    - [Recognition Signal](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-signal/): Recognition Signal: Information that helps a system correctly identify and recall a brand.
    - [Recognition Triangle](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/recognition-triangle/): Recognition Triangle: The three conditions of recognition: Clarity, Credibility, and Earned Authority.
    - [Structural Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/recognition-authority/structural-authority/): Structural Authority is the Earned Authority layer built from structural sources: Wikipedia, industry databases, knowledge graphs, and schema markup.
  - [AI-Mediated Discovery](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/): How discovery is changing: AI-Mediated Discovery, AI visibility, AI recommendations and referrals, answer engines, conversational search, zero-click search, agentic discovery, AI Overviews, and AI Mode, defined in plain language.
    - [Agentic Discovery](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/agentic-discovery/): Agentic Discovery: AI agents that evaluate and act on options on a person's behalf.
    - [AI-Mediated Discovery](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-mediated-discovery/): AI-Mediated Discovery: Discovery that happens through AI systems interpreting information on a person's behalf.
    - [AI Mode](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-mode/): AI Mode is Google's conversational AI search experience, which uses query fan-out to research a question across multiple searches before generating a response.
    - [AI Overviews](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-overviews/): AI Overviews are Google's AI-generated summaries that appear above traditional search results for some queries, drawing on and citing a range of web sources.
    - [AI Recommendation](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-recommendation/): AI Recommendation: When an AI system puts a brand forward as an option worth considering.
    - [AI Referral](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-referral/): AI Referral: When an AI answer points someone onward to a brand's site or resource.
    - [AI Search](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-search/): AI Search: Search experiences that generate an answer rather than a list of links.
    - [AI Visibility](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/ai-visibility/): AI Visibility: How often and where a brand appears in AI-generated answers.
    - [Answer Eligibility](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/answer-eligibility/): Answer Eligibility: Whether a source is even in the running to be used in an answer.
    - [Answer Engine](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/answer-engine/): An answer engine is a search or AI system built to return a direct answer to a question rather than a ranked list of pages for the user to evaluate themselves.
    - [Conversational Search](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/conversational-search/): Conversational Search: Search as a back-and-forth, where later questions build on earlier ones.
    - [Zero-Click Search](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-mediated-discovery/zero-click-search/): Zero-Click Search: When the answer is delivered without the user visiting the source.
  - [Retrieval, Evidence & Consensus](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/): How an AI system's understanding of a brand forms: retrieval, retrievability, query fan-out, source selection and diversity, corroboration, provenance, citation, consensus, model consensus, signal consistency, grounding, and RAG.
    - [Canonical Source](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/canonical-source/): Canonical Source: The version of a fact a system treats as authoritative.
    - [Citation](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/citation/): A citation is a reference to a brand, source, or piece of information that an AI system or search engine uses, and often surfaces, when constructing an answer.
    - [Citation Decay](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/citation-decay/): Citation Decay: References becoming fewer, less prominent, or out of date over time.
    - [Consensus](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/consensus/): Consensus is the degree to which independent sources, and increasingly independent AI systems, arrive at the same understanding of a brand.
    - [Corroboration](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/corroboration/): Corroboration happens when independent sources provide consistent evidence supporting the same understanding of a brand, claim, or fact.
    - [Entity Consistency](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/entity-consistency/): Entity Consistency: Being represented the same way as an entity across the ecosystem.
    - [Grounding](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/grounding/): Grounding is how an AI system connects a generated response to external, verifiable information, rather than relying only on patterns learned during training.
    - [Information Provenance](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/information-provenance/): Information provenance is the traceable origin and history of a piece of information: where a claim came from, and what sources support it.
    - [Model Consensus](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/model-consensus/): Model Consensus: Different AI systems agreeing on what a brand is and is known for.
    - [Query Fan-Out](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/query-fan-out/): Query Fan-Out: Breaking one question into many searches before answering.
    - [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/rag/): Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Retrieving source material before generating an answer.
    - [Retrievability](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/retrievability/): Retrievability: The degree to which a brand's information can actually be found and used.
    - [Retrieval](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/retrieval/): Retrieval is the process an AI system uses to find relevant information from available sources before generating a response.
    - [Signal Consistency](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/signal-consistency/): Signal Consistency: Whether the evidence around a brand tells the same story everywhere.
    - [Source Diversity](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/source-diversity/): Source Diversity: The range of independent sources feeding a system's understanding.
    - [Source Selection](https://aingworth.com/glossary/retrieval-evidence-consensus/source-selection/): Source selection is how a search or AI system decides which of the available sources are relevant and trustworthy enough to use when constructing an answer.
  - [Search, SEO & Generative Optimization](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/): The established disciplines defined honestly: SEO, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), semantic search and optimization, entity recognition and authority, knowledge graphs, structured data, schema markup, and E-E-A-T.
    - [Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/aeo/): Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Structuring content so answer engines can extract and use it.
    - [E-E-A-T](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/eeat/): E-E-A-T: Google's Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness framework.
    - [Entity Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/entity-authority/): Entity Authority: The strength and consistency of the signals tied to an entity.
    - [Entity Recognition](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/entity-recognition/): Entity recognition is the process by which a system identifies and classifies real-world things, such as a person, brand, or place, within text or data.
    - [Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/geo/): Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Optimizing content for representation in generative AI environments.
    - [Knowledge Graph](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/knowledge-graph/): Knowledge Graph: A structured map of entities and how they relate.
    - [Schema Markup](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/schema-markup/): Schema Markup: A structured data vocabulary added to a page to disambiguate it.
    - [Semantic Optimization](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/semantic-optimization/): Semantic Optimization: Structuring content so its meaning, not just its keywords, is clear.
    - [Semantic Search](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/semantic-search/): Semantic search is a search approach that interprets the meaning and intent behind a query, rather than matching keywords alone.
    - [Search Engine Optimization (SEO)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/seo/): Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Improving a site so search engines can index, understand, and rank it.
    - [Structured Data](https://aingworth.com/glossary/search-seo-generative-optimization/structured-data/): Structured Data: Information formatted so machines can read it directly.
  - [AI & Search Infrastructure](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/): The technical vocabulary behind AI search interfaces: large language models, generative AI, natural language processing, machine learning, embeddings, vector search, context windows, tokens, entities, and AI hallucination.
    - [AI Hallucination](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/ai-hallucination/): An AI hallucination is inaccurate or fabricated output produced by an AI system and presented as though it were fact.
    - [Context Window](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/context-window/): A context window is the amount of text an AI model can consider at one time when generating a response.
    - [Embeddings](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/embeddings/): Embeddings: Numerical representations that place similar meanings close together.
    - [Entity](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/entity/): Entity: A distinct, identifiable thing a system can recognize and connect.
    - [Generative AI](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/generative-ai/): Generative AI refers to AI systems that create new content, such as text, images, or code, rather than only classifying or retrieving existing content.
    - [Large Language Model (LLM)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/llm/): Large Language Model (LLM): A model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
    - [Machine Learning](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/machine-learning/): Machine learning is a method of building AI systems where a model learns patterns from data, rather than following rules written explicitly by a person.
    - [Natural Language Processing (NLP)](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/nlp/): Natural Language Processing, or NLP, is the field of AI concerned with how machines understand, interpret, and generate human language.
    - [Token](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/token/): A token is a unit of text, often a word or part of a word, that an AI language model processes as its basic building block.
    - [Vector Search](https://aingworth.com/glossary/ai-search-infrastructure/vector-search/): Vector search is a search method that finds results by comparing embeddings for similarity in meaning, rather than matching exact keywords.
  - [Content & Authority Strategy](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/): What a brand actually builds to earn recognition: topical authority, content architecture and clusters, content depth, internal linking, first-party content, third-party evidence, digital PR, trust signals, and entity signals.
    - [Content Architecture](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/content-architecture/): Content Architecture: How content is structured and connected so it can be navigated.
    - [Content Clusters](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/content-clusters/): Content Clusters: Groups of linked content organized around a core topic.
    - [Content Depth](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/content-depth/): Content Depth: How thoroughly a piece of content actually covers its subject.
    - [Digital PR](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/digital-pr/): Digital PR: Earning coverage and mentions from independent publications.
    - [Entity Signals](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/entity-signals/): Entity Signals: The information that helps a system identify a brand correctly.
    - [First-Party Content](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/first-party-content/): First-Party Content: What a brand publishes about itself, on channels it controls.
    - [Internal Linking](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/internal-linking/): Internal Linking: Linking between a site's own pages to show how they relate.
    - [Third-Party Evidence](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/third-party-evidence/): Third-Party Evidence: Evidence about a brand from sources it does not control.
    - [Topical Authority](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/topical-authority/): Topical Authority: Demonstrated depth across a subject rather than a single page.
    - [Trust Signals](https://aingworth.com/glossary/content-authority-strategy/trust-signals/): Trust Signals: The cues that help people and systems judge reliability.
  - [Measurement & AI Visibility](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/): How to tell whether recognition is improving: AI visibility measurement, citation share, answer share, share of voice, AI referral traffic, brand mentions, recognition measurement, and authority measurement.
    - [AI Referral Traffic](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/ai-referral-traffic/): AI referral traffic is website traffic that arrives from a link included in an AI-generated response, rather than from a traditional search results page.
    - [AI Visibility Measurement](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/ai-visibility-measurement/): AI Visibility Measurement: Tracking how, where, and how often a brand appears in AI answers.
    - [Answer Share](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/answer-share/): Answer share is the proportion of AI-generated answers on a given topic in which a particular brand appears at all, whether cited, named, or recommended.
    - [Authority Measurement](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/authority-measurement/): Authority Measurement: Tracking the strength and consistency of a brand's evidence over time.
    - [Brand Mention](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/brand-mention/): Brand Mention: Any instance of a brand being named or referenced.
    - [Citation Share](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/citation-share/): Citation share is the proportion of AI-generated answers on a given topic that cite a particular brand, relative to its competitors.
    - [Recognition Measurement](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/recognition-measurement/): Recognition Measurement: Tracking whether a brand is described accurately, not just mentioned.
    - [Share of Voice](https://aingworth.com/glossary/measurement-ai-visibility/share-of-voice/): Share of Voice: A brand's proportion of visibility within its category.
- [The Frameworks](https://aingworth.com/frameworks/): The seven named frameworks from Become the Answer, each with an extractable definition: the Recognition Triangle, the Authority Method, the Machine Gatekeeper, Authority Debt, the Recognition Economy, the Composite Picture, and brand hallucination.
- [Our Approach](https://aingworth.com/approach/): The thesis behind the practice and how the Authority Method is applied.
- [The Book](https://aingworth.com/book/): Become the Answer: How Brands Build Authority in the Age of AI, by Lucy Aingworth, available on Amazon.
- [HER-Worth](https://aingworth.com/her-worth/): A separate consulting and coaching program founded by Lucy Aingworth for women founders and executives.
- [About Lucy Aingworth](https://aingworth.com/about/): Lucy's background, expertise, and the convictions behind Aingworth's practice.
- [Contact](https://aingworth.com/contact/): Direct contact form for consulting, speaking, media, HER-Worth, or general enquiries.
- [Recognition Check](https://aingworth.com/recognition-check/): The Recognition Check runs one buyer question across the AI models several times and measures how consistently they name you. See your Recognition Rate, and what AI always, sometimes, and rarely says.
- [Recognition Snapshot](https://aingworth.com/recognition-snapshot/): The Recognition Snapshot is Aingworth's paid audit: a structured, one-time read of how AI systems see your brand today across Clarity, Credibility, and Earned Authority. Formerly called the AI Visibility Audit. $1,500, five to ten business days.
- [Case Studies](https://aingworth.com/case-studies/): Real results across SEO, paid social and conversion, from one consultant reading them as a single system. Named client work by Lucy Aingworth of Aingworth.

## Articles

- [Articles on AI Visibility & Brand Authority](https://aingworth.com/articles/): Articles on AI search visibility, generative engine optimization, and brand authority from Lucy Aingworth. Practical thinking, evidence first.
  - [The AI Risk Debate: What's Documented and What's Still a Guess](https://aingworth.com/articles/documented-modeled-or-guessed/): Four AI safety experts gave four different extinction odds from the same evidence. Here is how to sort what is documented, what is modeled, and what is guessed.
  - [Machines Don't Browse. They Extract.](https://aingworth.com/articles/machines-dont-browse-they-extract/): AI systems don't browse your site, they extract fragments and reassemble them. Content architecture decides what gets pulled out and cited.
  - [AI-Generated Reports Are Getting Faster. Verification Is Not Keeping Up.](https://aingworth.com/articles/fastest-report-least-checked/): New 2026 survey data shows employees feeding client and financial data into public AI tools at scale, while executives catch AI-generated errors only after they reach the board. What changes, and what does not.
  - [The Stakes Test: Why Credibility Decides High-Value Deals](https://aingworth.com/articles/the-stakes-test/): The more a decision costs to get wrong, the harder the buyer leans on proof over claims. Founders and executives sit at the high-stakes end, and so does the way AI treats them.
  - [You Are Using AI in the Wrong Place](https://aingworth.com/articles/using-ai-in-the-wrong-place/): Most AI spend misses because the constraint was never the visible, repetitive work. For most founders and executives the real block is recognition. No automation reaches it.
  - [Being Cited Is Not Being Chosen](https://aingworth.com/articles/being-cited-is-not-being-chosen/): Almost half of consumers now ask AI to find a local business, but only 18 percent act on the answer without checking it elsewhere. The verification step, not the citation, is where the decision is made.
  - [AI Visibility Is a Range, Not a Number](https://aingworth.com/articles/your-ai-visibility-score-is-a-fiction/): Personalized AI answers make position a per-user variable. A single AI visibility score describes one person's experience as though it described everyone's. What to report instead.
  - [When the Gatekeeper Starts Acting](https://aingworth.com/articles/when-the-gatekeeper-starts-acting/): Agentic AI completes tasks end to end, narrowing the field at a step no human reads. Being uncited is no longer the only way to lose, and the new failure mode leaves no trace.
  - [The Technical Work That Pays](https://aingworth.com/articles/the-technical-work-that-pays/): A four hundred item technical audit is a way of looking thorough. Three questions decide whether a machine can comprehend your business at all, and most of the checklist answers none of them.
  - [There Is No Algorithm to Chase](https://aingworth.com/articles/there-is-no-algorithm-to-chase/): Core updates now roll continuously and without announcement. When the target moves silently, reactive optimization stops being a strategy and becomes a superstition.
  - [Every Brand Has an AI Biography](https://aingworth.com/articles/every-brand-has-an-ai-biography/): Your AI biography is the story machines tell about your business when you are not in the room. How it is built, how it goes wrong, and how to change it.
  - [The GEO Gold Rush: Why Most AI Visibility Advice Is Wrong](https://aingworth.com/articles/the-geo-gold-rush/): Most AI visibility advice is built on assumption, not evidence. What the research actually shows about llms.txt, schema, content volume, and what really drives AI citations.

## Research

- [The Research Behind Become the Answer](https://aingworth.com/research/): Independent research behind the Recognition Triangle: what actually moves AI citations, who gets cited and how often, and how many people now ask AI instead of searching. Every figure sourced and dated.
  - [How the Machine Gatekeeper Decides](https://aingworth.com/research/machine-gatekeeper/): What actually determines whether an AI system cites you: a 129,000-domain study on citation factors, Google's own statement on AI optimization, and why blocking AI crawlers is self-sabotage.
  - [The Evidence Behind Earned Authority](https://aingworth.com/research/earned-authority/): What actually earns AI citations: a 680-million-citation index showing fifty domains decide most of what AI says about brands, why Reddit outranks every news outlet, and why WSJ, NYT, and Bloomberg don't make the top twenty.
  - [The Evidence Behind the Recognition Economy](https://aingworth.com/research/recognition-economy/): Evidence that the shift from being seen to being recognized is real and still moving: AI chatbot adoption data, a citation landscape splitting across four engines, and how Google itself is rebuilding search around named answers.

## Playbooks

- [Playbooks: How to Build Recognition, Step by Step](https://aingworth.com/playbooks/): Doable, step-by-step guides for building AI recognition yourself: reading your own Recognition Triangle, closing an Earned Authority gap, and writing pages a machine can cite. From Aingworth, the company behind Become the Answer.
  - [How to Read Your Own Recognition Triangle](https://aingworth.com/playbooks/read-your-own-recognition-triangle/): A twenty-minute, doable-yourself process for checking your Clarity, Credibility, and Earned Authority before you book anything. A playbook from Aingworth.
